rationale: Three lenses ran with parseable output (blind, edge-case, acceptance against the ticket's 5 ACs plus the specific review finding note_2466282); no decision_needed finding remains, so confidence is high despite request-changes. Three blocking findings survive triage: an unguarded negative-duration path (new CASE expression does not follow this same file's own established ended_at>=started_at clamp convention used for subagent duration_ms, and the gap propagates unclamped through reader.py and the handler), an unguarded ::boolean cast on client-supplied JSON that can raise and fail the whole session's rollup query (confirmed: no other ::boolean cast exists anywhere else in rollups.py, so this is not an accepted existing pattern), and a documented-tolerance paragraph that overstates its own guarantee (AC3) by not disclosing that a session sending no further raw telemetry after its last Stop never gets the 'closing' event the text promises -- the ticket's own primary reported scenario. This also makes AC2/AC3 partial, not pass. One additional concern (the provisional-summary branch now re-running the full, multi-column fb LATERAL on every Stop for new-plugin clients, not just when due) is real but unmeasured here; included as a finding since the mechanism change is concrete and the affected path is common, not rare. Deferred (1, pre-existing, not this change's job): the other session_dims counters (turns, tool_calls, cost/token sums) still use the plain summary-or-fallback rule with no provisional-is-a-lower-bound treatment -- this diff narrowed the fix to duration only, by design, and did not introduce or worsen that gap. Dismissed (4, below the floor or not newly introduced): unconditional trust in client-supplied is_final with no reconciliation (inherent to the pre-existing summary mechanism, not new); a naming inversion (fallback_duration holds the preferred value, not the fallback) -- cosmetic; external review-note IDs baked into source comments -- cosmetic; get_repository_sessions's max(session_duration_ms) across grouped rows -- reasonable by exact analogy to the pre-existing max(started_at)/max(last_event_at) pattern, no concrete trigger shown. One blind-lens item ('new test file has no actual code') was a false positive caused by the orchestrator's own abbreviated dispatch prompt (an English summary was substituted for the real diff body to keep the blind-lens prompt short) and is not counted.

business_review.item: AC1: Normal /exit reliably records session completion
business_review.notes: Backend-only diff; the CLI hook sender lives in a separate repository (codemie-code) not present here. Pre-accepted as out of scope for a backend-only fix per this task's own technical-analysis.md; nothing in this diff changes that boundary.

business_review.item: AC2: Missing/cancelled SessionEnd does not truncate session duration
business_review.notes: The new greatest(summary.ended_at, fb.last_ts) widening fixes the case where some later raw record exists after the last Stop. A session that sends zero further raw telemetry after its last Stop (the ticket's own primary reported shape) still has duration cut at that Stop's timestamp -- the fix narrows the bug's frequency but does not close it for this specific, common shape.

business_review.item: AC3: Session duration matches actual session lifetime within documented tolerance
business_review.notes: A tolerance paragraph was added to cli-analytics-storage.md, satisfying the letter of 'documented'. But its wording ('closed by the next raw event or summary, whichever lands first') implies the gap always eventually closes, which is false for a session with no further telemetry after its last Stop -- see CR-003.
Only ended_at/activity_started_at/duration_ms expressions and the provisional-summary join predicate are touched; no cost/token/request/turn/tool counter in rollups.py is modified by this diff.

business_review.item: AC5: Automated coverage includes repeated normal exits and cancelled SessionEnd fallback behavior
business_review.notes: test_live_session_duration_fallback.py covers non-final-summary widening, final-summary authority, and stability across repeated rollup refreshes (the 'repeated' half, as recomputation, not repeated CLI exits -- pre-accepted out of scope). No test exercises the fully-idle-after-last-Stop case where the fix's own mechanism cannot widen the duration -- exactly the gap in AC2/AC3 above.

business_review.item: Review note_2466282: a non-final (is_final:false) summary must be treated as a provisional lower bound combined with the latest raw record, not authoritative
business_review.notes: _IS_FINAL_SUMMARY/_PROVISIONAL_SUMMARY and the _ENDED_AT CASE expression implement exactly this; a final summary (or absent is_final) stays authoritative outright, a provisional one is combined via greatest(...) with fb.last_ts, and _FALLBACK_DUE was extended with OR _PROVISIONAL_SUMMARY so fb.last_ts is actually computed in that case.

business_review.item: Review note_2466282: AC3's documented tolerance must state where the undercount is bounded and by what
business_review.notes: Same gap as AC3 above: the documented bound is only real when a later event eventually arrives; the idle-tail case is not disclosed as unbounded.

standards_review.notes: Committed as 'EPMCDME-15584: Make a non-final session summary provisional for duration', matching the project's 'EPMCDME-<id>: <imperative summary>' convention, with the required Generated with AI / Co-Authored-By trailers.
ruff format --check and ruff check both clean on the changed files per two independent verification passes (implementer and independent audit).

No auth, secrets, or injection-relevant code touched. The ::boolean cast issue (CR-002) is a reliability/robustness defect (an unhandled malformed-input error path), not an auth/injection/secrets issue, so it is reported as a correctness finding, not flagged here.

findings.title: duration_ms has no ended_at>=started_at guard
findings.problem: The new _ENDED_AT/_ACTIVITY_STARTED_AT/_DURATION_MS expressions compute duration_ms = ms_between(_ENDED_AT, _ACTIVITY_STARTED_AT) with no guard against ended_at preceding activity_started_at (clock skew between a summary's own ended_at and fb.last_ts, or malformed client attrs). This same file already establishes the right convention for exactly this risk, just for subagent duration_ms: 'CASE WHEN tm.ended_at >= tm.started_at THEN ms_between(...) END' (around the _SUBAGENT_VALUES duration_ms entry). The new session-level computation does not follow it. The negative value then flows unclamped through reader.py's three duration_ms read sites (get_session_durations's coalesce, get_session_detail_meta's coalesce, get_session_cost_facts's max(session_duration_ms)) and into cli_analytics_handler.py's get_sessions, whose new preferred branch ('duration_ms = _i(fallback_duration)') has no max(0, ...) clamp even though its own sibling hook-pair branch does.
findings.impact: A negative session duration can reach session_dims, the session list/detail REST responses, and the overview KPI sum/avg aggregations, visibly corrupting a user-facing number and silently understating duration totals and averages.
findings.recommendation: Add the same guard this file already uses for subagent duration_ms: wrap duration_ms's computation in 'CASE WHEN <ended> >= <started> THEN ... END' at the source in rollups.py, and additionally clamp with greatest(0, ...) at the reader.py/handler.py read sites for defense in depth, matching cli_analytics_handler.py's own existing max(0, ...) convention on its hook-pair branch.

findings.title: is_final cast can throw on malformed attrs
findings.problem: _IS_FINAL_SUMMARY = "coalesce((...->>'is_final')::boolean, true)" casts a raw JSON text value straight to ::boolean with no validation. Postgres's boolean cast accepts only a fixed set of literal spellings; any other value (a malformed attrs blob, an unexpected representation such as "1"/"0", or a future client sending something else under this key) raises 'invalid input syntax for type boolean' at query-build/execution time. This is not an existing, accepted pattern in this file: a grep of rollups.py confirms this is the only ::boolean cast anywhere in it, so there is no established convention this follows -- it is new, unguarded surface this diff introduces.
findings.impact: A single session with a malformed or unexpected is_final value fails the entire session_dims recompute query for that batch, which (per this file's own _COUNTER_JOINS/_COUNTER_VALUES structure) likely aborts the whole rollup refresh pass rather than just that one session's row, stalling duration (and every other summary counter) for every session in the batch.
findings.recommendation: Validate before casting, e.g. CASE WHEN ({_booleans('sm.attrs')}->>'is_final') IN ('true','false') THEN (...)::boolean ELSE true END, or coalesce(nullif(...,'')::boolean, true) only after confirming the value is a valid boolean literal.

findings.title: documented tolerance overstates its own guarantee
findings.problem: The new tolerance paragraph says the undercount is 'closed by the next raw event or summary, whichever lands first, and by the real SessionEnd once it arrives' -- phrasing that implies closure is guaranteed to eventually happen. It does not disclose that a session which sends zero further raw telemetry after its last Stop (the ticket's own primary reported scenario: a normal /exit with a cancelled SessionEnd and no further activity) never receives such a closing event, so the undercount in that specific, common case is not actually bounded by anything this mechanism provides -- duration stays at the last Stop's timestamp indefinitely, same as before this fix.
findings.impact: AC3 asks for a documented tolerance; as written, the tolerance misrepresents its own limits for exactly the scenario the ticket exists to fix, which could mislead whoever next reads this guide (or the reviewer/PO closing AC3) into believing the gap is always self-correcting.
findings.recommendation: State the idle-tail case explicitly: while only a provisional summary has been seen and no further raw/summary event ever arrives, the undercount is not bounded by this mechanism and persists until one does -- matching the honest framing already written into this task's own qa-report.md addendum, which should be carried into the user-facing guide, not left only in the internal QA record.

findings.title: fb LATERAL now runs on every provisional summary, not only when due
findings.problem: WHERE ({_FALLBACK_DUE}) OR {_PROVISIONAL_SUMMARY} makes the fb LATERAL subquery -- which computes the raw-range scan across hook_events/usage_requests/log_events/spans/metric_points plus file counts, tool-error counts, and compaction extraction -- run whenever the latest summary is merely provisional. Per this diff's own new documentation, every Stop on codemie-code >=0.15.9 sends a provisional (is_final:false) summary, so this is now the common case for any client running that version, not a rare fallback path. The surrounding comment itself notes only fb.last_ts is actually used in the provisional branch; every other fb.* column computed there is wasted work.
findings.impact: Rollup refresh cost for an in-progress session on a current-version client goes up on effectively every recompute (every Stop), not only in the pre-existing rare fallback case -- a real, unmeasured performance regression risk for the refresh pipeline at scale, analogous in kind (though not yet measured in magnitude) to the concrete timing regression found and fixed in the sibling EPMCDME-15582 MR's own review this same day.
findings.recommendation: Either benchmark this specific change under realistic session/log volume before merging, or narrow the provisional-summary branch to compute only last_ts (e.g. a lighter query path) instead of the full fb LATERAL's other columns, which are confirmed unused in that branch.
